_about: Published prices for the add-ons a traveller can put on the bill: wifi, seat choice, an extra-legroom seat, priority boarding, a lounge day pass, and travel insurance as a share of the ticket. Researched from the airlines' own pages and re-checked by a second reader (2026-09-25, per Patrick). build.py inlines only the prices; the sources stay here.
_method: Keyed by the airline flying the longest flight. Each row has a 'long' and a 'short' price in US cents (short-haul: a trip inside one border, or no flight over four hours). 'from': true marks a published starting price (the airline's cheapest), which the page still marks with its estimate asterisk. 'free': a sentence when the airline gives it away (to everyone, or to members of its free loyalty programme). Foreign-currency prices are converted at the rate on the as_of date and say so. A figure with no primary source is left out, and the page falls back to its typical price, marked.

priority.note: Most airlines' pages refuse automated readers; the readable ones (Frontier, TAP) are in 'prices'.

_not_readable: 2026-09-25: the lounge and boarding pages of American, United, British Airways, Lufthansa, Air France, KLM, Iberia, Aer Lingus, Turkish, Icelandair and Wizz refuse automated readers, and the Internet Archive was not reachable from this session, so those airlines stay on the typical price, marked. A person with a browser can read them.
_method_2026_09_25: Second pass, 2026-09-25 (per Patrick: the airline pages refuse automated readers or print no price, so find the price another way). Five research agents read the airlines' own pages where they could and dated secondary reports where they could not (The Points Guy, NerdWallet, Upgraded Points, One Mile at a Time, Head for Points, Simple Flying and the like); a second agent opened every source and confirmed, corrected or rejected each figure (163 confirmed, 9 corrected, 17 rejected). 'reported': true marks a figure only a secondary source states; 'seen': true marks the airline's own price read from its seat map through Duffel on sample flights (10 Nov 2026, economy, one way); 'low'/'high' give the range a source states, with 'cents' its midpoint or typical figure. All of these keep the asterisk: they are this airline's usual price, not this flight's. Foreign prices are converted at the ECB reference rate of 2026-09-25 (the dirham and the riyal at their dollar pegs); '_was' keeps the original.
